in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. His name is Alex and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex!

To continue assessing your eligibility, I have a few more questions.

Are you responsible for Alex? This generally means he lives with you, or you're contributing towards the cost of looking after him (at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't live with me actually. But I do help out financially - I contribute towards his costs each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the situation a bit more.

Does Alex live with someone else who is also claiming (or planning to claim) Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum claims Child Benefit for him and he lives with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. This is helpful information.

Since Alex lives with his mum and she is already claiming Child Benefit for him, I have one more question to clarify the situation:

How much do you contribute towards Alex's costs each week? And is this amount at least equal to the current Child Benefit rate (which is £25.60 per week for a first child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £10 a week - I help out with things like clothes and bits and pieces for him. So no, it's not as much as the Child Benefit rate.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me and the UK government rules, I need to let you know that unfortunately, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex in your current circumstances.

Here's why:

1. **Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child** - Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

2. **To be considered "responsible" for a child who doesn't live with you**, you need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate (currently £25.60 per week for a first child) towards their upkeep.

3. Since you're contributing around £10 per week, this is less than the Child Benefit rate, so you wouldn't meet the threshold to be considered responsible for Alex under the eligibility rules.

If you wanted to claim Child Benefit for Alex, you would need to either:
- Increase your contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate, **and** agree with Alex's mum about who should claim (since only one person can receive it), or
- Have Alex come to live with you

Let me now formally record this eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've completed my assessment. To summarise:

**You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

The key reasons are:
- Alex lives with his mother, who is already claiming Child Benefit for him
- Your weekly contribution of approximately £10 is below the £25.60 per week threshold needed to be considered "responsible" for a child who doesn't live with you
- Only one person can receive Child Benefit for any given child

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you increase your contributions and come to an agreement with his mother about who should claim—you may wish to revisit your eligibility.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
